speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: So. You're the one they sent through the old tunnel. Kettle's been on since noon.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I was told someone would come past the dry spring and that grumpy Warden. Not who. Certainly not this damp.
new_text: I was told someone would come past the dry spring and that grumpy Warden. Nobody mentioned I'd need to wring them out.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: This isn't trust, dearie. You could be anyone's spy, and whoever pushed you into that tunnel is reckless. I don't like reckless.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: But a body in that state needs a bed, and I have far too much pie. Welcome to {town}. Questions later.

speaker: The Wanderer
current_text: ...I don't remember who I am. Not sure I'm worth the bed.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: Hm. Then we start with tea and pie and work up from there.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: First, get yourself known. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back and knock.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A narrow gap in the old treeline - easy to miss, easy enough to slip through, if you're not afraid of a shortcut.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: {town}

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Hm. You came back. Wrote it in the notebook: 'came back.' Best two words I know.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Gate stays open. Always is. My girl's still up that road somewhere. In case.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Hm. That road. The Capital. You want to know why nobody comes back.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. {villain} chained all four.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: So now it's Blackout, Famine, Restless Dead and Clutter up there. Dark streets, slow legs, no food that heals, rubbish in your deck.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: You could walk in today. You would not walk far. Free the four zones: each one you free turns one service back on.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: My girl Isla went up that road eight years ago. If you see her... tell her the gate is still open.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Hm. Services still broken. Count them on the board by the road.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Every zone you free puts one back. Then that castle door gets a lot less scary. My knees stay scary. Nothing to be done.
new_text: Hm, each freed zone restores a service and makes the castle less frightening. My knees remain a local problem.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Hm. All four zones free. The lights are on up there. I can see them from here.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
current_text: Go on. Knock on that castle door. Hard. And if you see Isla... I'm still watching the road.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The castle door is cold to the touch. With the city's services still broken, whatever waits inside will have every advantage.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: You can go in. You probably should not. Yet.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: You did it. Grandmaster Flex is out. He made me stretch for forty minutes. I cried twice. Good tears.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: The bridge stays down now. I oil the crank every morning anyway. It's a love thing.
new_text: The bridge stays down now, but I still oil the crank every morning. Maintenance is how I say sorry.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: Want to spar? Gently. I'll spot you. I'm a spotter. ...I'm SO glad I can say that quietly.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: Brick Bronson cracks his knuckles, grabs the crank, and lowers the bridge with one arm. Show-off.

speaker: Brick Bronson
current_text: The planks thump down across the gorge. The Gainlands are open.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The afterlife is processing again. Agnes says the queue moved four whole numbers yesterday. We had cake.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: I have a new stamp. It says HELPED. I have used it nine times. I am counting.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: You may challenge me again, if you like. No permit required. That one is my favourite rule.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The barrier is down. A sign with a stamp on it says the road needs a permit. Nobody has ever been issued one.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: Prudence Pallor stamps a permit, hands it over, and files the original in triplicate.

speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor
current_text: The barrier creaks up. The road to the D.N.A. is open.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: She's back. The real Grand Chef. She tasted my soup and said 'more salt' and I have never been so happy.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The pantry door stays open now. Wide open. People wander in and eat biscuits. That is the dream.
new_text: The pantry door stays wide open, and people come in for biscuits. At last, a proper open-door pastry.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: A friendly duel? For old times' sake. Loser washes the ladle. It is a very big ladle.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: An enormous pantry door blocks the lane. Locked. The keyhole is the size of a dinner plate.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: Chef Fennel Gravois hands over a key the size of a ladle. It turns with a satisfying clunk.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
current_text: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: Archdruid Compostella is herself again. She hugged me. She smells like rain and a little bit like compost. Perfect.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: The thorns are gone. Mostly. I keep one in a pot. It's very well behaved now.
new_text: Most of the thorns are gone; I keep one in a pot. It's behaving, but I'm not ready to let it meet the curtains.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: Want a practice round? I promise not to thorn at you. Much. The raccoons are judging, so be nice.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: A wall of thorns has swallowed the forest path. It looks like it is breathing.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: Moss Mulligan lays a hand on the thorns. They sigh, brown, and crumble into leaf mould.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
current_text: The forest path to the Verdant Dump is open.

speaker: Sable
current_text: Well met, {wanderer}. Sable, darling: seller of cards, and of very good stories about cards.

speaker: Sable
current_text: You start with plain neutral cards. The Paths are where the power is. Browse, buy, then put it all to work at the Deck Station.

speaker: Sable
current_text: Where do my cards come from? The past. Next question. My prices are fair, mostly. {villain}'s taxes are not.

speaker: Sable
current_text: Back, darling? Everything on the table is honest. Mostly. The misprints are lying, but so charmingly.
new_text: Back, darling? The cards are honest; the misprints simply have a more adventurous relationship with spelling.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
current_text: Hi! Hello! You look like you need supplies! Tilly Tonic! I'm teal today, which means the new batch works!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
current_text: Everything here is one use in a fight! Equip what you buy on your Character screen, then use it on your turn!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
current_text: Probably not on yourself! Unless it's a healing one! I tested the healing one! I'm fine! I'm green! I'm usually green!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
current_text: Back! Potions! Charms! I'm a bit orange today, so maybe not the orange one! Equip them on your Character screen to carry them into a fight!
new_text: Potions and charms, back for more! Equip them on your Character screen for fights - maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The door rattles. Something behind it is muttering about a receipt.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Whatever it is, it is not open for business.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: OooOOOooo. Who disturbs the store room? We are VERY busy haunting it.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Ninety years ago the three of us bought one lantern between us. It never worked. Tilly's great-grandmother said: no receipt, no refund.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: So we waited. Then we died. Then we kept waiting. Professionally.
new_text: We waited, died, and kept waiting. Your haunting is very important to us.
writer_note: Customer-service hold-message parody; retains the ghosts' sequence and shared grievance.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: ...You're haunting a shop over a lantern.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: A FAULTY lantern. Four copper. With ninety years' interest, it is still four copper. We did the maths. We had time.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Nobody comes in until it is refunded. Or until somebody beats us at cards. Everyone settles everything with cards round here.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: ...Fine. FINE. You play like someone who kept the receipt.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: We'll go. The chapel belfry has a lovely draught and nobody has complained about it in centuries.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Tell Tilly the lantern is on the top shelf. It still doesn't work. We checked. Every night. For ninety years.
new_text: Tell Tilly the lantern's on the top shelf, still broken after ninety years of nightly checks. We were thorough, if poorly lit.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Ha! No refund, no entry. Come back with a better deck. Or a receipt. Ideally both.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Just shelves now. And one broken lantern on the top shelf, exactly where they said it would be.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Halt. Equipment is issued on referral only. Security Protocol Two. Elder Maren does the referring.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Come back with her blessing. And better posture. Mostly the blessing.
new_text: Bring Elder Maren's blessing. Better posture is appreciated but cannot be accepted in its place.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Elder Maren sent you. I could tell from your gait. It says 'referred'. Congratulations: your file is now thick enough to be a file.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Before I issue gear, protocol asks for exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight. A roamer, a gatekeeper, a dungeon, the arena. I will know.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Then come back and I will hand you something pointy.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: One fight won. That is the whole requirement. So far I count zero. I am very good at counting to zero.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Go win a fight. Any fight. I will be here, guarding the drawer.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: One fight, won. Stamp. Stamp. Stamp. Three stamps is the correct number of stamps.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: Your Starter Blade. The first unit you play each battle hits a little harder. Do not run with it.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: And all five equipment slots are yours now: helm, weapon, armor, boots, relic.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
current_text: The good stuff is rarer, and you can only wear so much of it until you level up. Protocol. Fact: bears do not wear helms. Bears are wiser than us.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: The Undercroft

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: A cellar hatch beside the old cottage, chained shut. Someone has scratched two little crossed swords into the wood.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: Whatever is down there is not open for business. Yet.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: Word around the square: the abandoned cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started roaring at night.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: From the cellar. Somebody brave should check the hatch. Somebody like you.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: WELCOME, CHAMPION, to THE UNDERCROFT! Mind the stairs. (Really. The third one bites.) I am Announcer Grand Bellows, KEEPER OF THE SAND!
new_text: WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION - ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! Mind the third stair; it bites without an introduction.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: For a thousand years the four Paths settled their rivalries in the old arena, until {villain} chained the doors. SO WE DUG.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: Since you freed a zone, THE RING IS OPEN! Battles and puzzles, tiers one to three, with prizes: ring-exclusive gear, gold, essence!

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: First clears pay out. Repeats are for GLORY. And for snacks. I brought snacks.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: THE SAND IS HOT! THE CEILING IS LOW! THE CROWD IS... mostly me, and a very good echo. Pick a fight, champion!
new_text: THE SAND IS HOT AND THE CEILING IS LOW! Pick a fight, champion - the crowd is mostly my echo, and he agrees with EVERYTHING!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
current_text: Something under the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road is open for business. Listen for the crowd.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Auntie Alembic's

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: The door of Auntie Alembic's is bolted. A note is pinned to it in green ink, in what looks like four handwritings at once:

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: 'CLOSED UNTIL TWO ZONES ARE FREE. {villain} TOOK MY CAULDRON. I AM BREWING IN THE SINK. THE SINK IS COPING. - A.'

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: With two zones free, a cauldron bubbles to life in {town}. Auntie Alembic's is open! Bring essence. Bring courage. Bring a fire blanket.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Auntie Alembic. Alchemist. Do not touch anything. ...Fine. Touch that one. It likes you.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Whenever you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, the extras turn into essence of that card's Path.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Bring me ALL the essence of two Paths, plus a little gold, and I will brew you a card of BOTH. Random. Unpredictable. Occasionally on fire.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: They say there was one spring once, the Wellspring, that fed all four Paths. Everything mixed at the source, dear. That is the kingdom I brew for.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Back already? Good. Essence of two Paths, a little gold, and a lot of faith. That is the whole recipe. Mind the red flask. It's listening.
new_text: Essence of two Paths and a little gold, dear; faith helps with the waiting. Lower your voice around the red flask - it takes things personally.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: You do not have enough essence of two different Paths yet. Collect more duplicates, then come back. The cauldron will wait.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: The cauldron is patient. The cauldron is also hungry.
new_text: The cauldron is patient. Please don't confuse patience with having had lunch.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
current_text: Auntie Alembic's, the Alchemist, is now open in {town}. Bring your leftovers.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: THE GAINLANDS ARE FREE!

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Chancellor Clench is down, Grandmaster Flex is back, and the weights are back in the gym. The mills turn at a sensible pace. Somewhere, Gary lifts something, and for once nobody has to spot him.
new_text: Chancellor Clench is down, Grandmaster Flex is back, and the weights are in the gym. The mills turn at a sensible pace; Gary lifts with a spotter.
writer_note: Story bible correction: freed Gary lifts with a spotter; preserves the other liberation facts.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: THE ENDLESS BUFFET IS FREE!

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Doppelganger is exposed, the Special Sauce is recalled, and the real Grand Chef is back in her kitchen. The golems guard plates again. Nobody leaves hungry.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: THE D.N.A. IS FREE!

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Mortimer Grimsby is removed from office, and the vacancy passes by policy to the senior-most applicant on file: Agnes Overdue. The Department of Necrotic Affairs belongs to itself again, and it is terrified by the freedom.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: THE VERDANT DUMP IS FREE!

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Rotheart is silent. The vines are only vines again. The Archdruid is herself and deeply apologetic about the barn. The land starts, slowly, to heal.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: %d of 4 zones free

speaker: (UI)
current_text: {villain} rules the four Paths through his rulers. Beat each road's gatekeeper, then free its zone by beating the boss of its main dungeon.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The imperial road to the Capital is open from the start, but its broken services will flatten you. Free the zones first. Gatekeeper Brannoch can explain.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: All four Paths are free. Buy cards, test yourself in the Undercroft, and brew something dangerous at the Alchemist's.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: {villain} has fallen and the Paths are free to mix. Build decks from three or four Paths at once, try the Alchemist's tri-Path crafting, test yourself in the Undercroft and visit the changed Capital.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Foil Fenwick

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Fenwick's Sealed Goods

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Psst. Over here. Do you hear that? ...That crinkle is the sound of possibility in a foil wrapper.
new_text: Psst... hear that crinkle? That's possibility, with excellent packaging.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods. Packs. Only packs. Open one in front of me and I will weep, so take it somewhere with better lighting.
new_text: Foil Fenwick, Purveyor of Sealed Goods - packs only. Open one where the light's good; if I cry, I want to see what I'm crying about.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: How it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. Lots of foil, no paperwork. The Necrocrats find it upsetting.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Free a zone and I stock its pack. Until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse! Sniff, if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: The crinkle returns! Browse. Sniff. Do not shake. ...Fine, shake a little.
new_text: Browse, sniff, but don't shake the packs. ...A little, then; I'm a collector, not a strong person.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Ah, a repeat customer. My favourite kind of customer. Also my only kind. Shh. Listen. ...Foil.
new_text: A repeat customer... shh, listen to that foil. You understand me, and I don't know what to do with that.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Fenwick pulls a curtain aside. "The back room. Prismatic packs: every Path in one wrapper.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: They only exist because the Paths are talking to each other again. Terrible for my exclusivity. Wonderful for my sales."

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Crinkle! A fine choice.
new_text: Crinkle! You've made a wrapper very happy.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Sealed, signed, and slightly warm.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: No refunds on bad luck. Bad luck is non-transferable.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: It wants to be opened. They always do.
new_text: It wants to be opened. I'm trying to respect its wishes without getting involved.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Gold, friend. The foil does not accept good intentions.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Not enough gold. The wrapper can tell.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
current_text: Not yet. That one is still a rumour in a wrapper.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Pip Threadwell

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Threadwell's Hats & Hems

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Try everything on. The mirror is polite; I am not.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Hat! Hat. Marvellous head. Hold still: your left shoulder is a size braver than your right.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Pip Threadwell, Haberdasher and Hemmer! Everything in here is purely cosmetic. It will not make you stronger, braver or better at card games.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: It will make you LOOK all three, which is eighty percent of the job. Try anything on in the little mirror first: hats up top, cloaks down the back, dye on both.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Free zones and climb levels, and I will find grander stock. I hear rumours of rarer pieces, too. People tell hatmakers everything.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Back for another look? Good. A person should change their mind and their hat regularly.
new_text: Back to change your mind and your hat? Excellent - one of those I can fit properly.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Ah, my favourite head! What are we doing today? Brim? Brooch? Billowing? Mind the pins. The pins mind nobody.
new_text: My favourite head, in the nick of time! Brim, brooch or billowing - this could be a hem-ergency.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Oh, you have been busy. New fabrics arrived. Do not ask where from. Some of them were yelling.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Stock has grown! Freed zones send me their finest fashions. Slightly singed, mostly fabulous.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Between us: a crown made of living leaves is growing in a bin somewhere in the Verdant Dump. And a cloak that has survived more than you have is draped over a chest on a muscly island.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone has to defeat the person who owns it first.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Gorgeous. Truly. You are going to turn heads, mostly in confusion.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Wear it out! Do not take it off in the rain. Or do. It is a hat, not a feelings machine.
new_text: Wear it out! A hat cannot have an entrance if you keep it in a bag!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Sold! Oh, the way it sits on you. Almost like it was sewn for another head entirely.
new_text: Sold! Such a dramatic fit - the hat looks surprised to be wearing you.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Gold, my dear head. Thread is not free, and neither is my charm.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: A little more gold, a little less hope. Come back when your pockets rustle.
new_text: A little more gold, my dear head. I can work wonders with fabric, but it insists on being paid for.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: Not yet. That one is still on the sewing table, and it is sulking.

speaker: Pip Threadwell
current_text: You already own that one. Wear it! Wear it twice!
new_text: You own that one already! Do introduce it to the outside world.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.
